# 0. What this file does

`Study5_02_Text.ipynb` measured the 12,042 justifications without seeing the
condition or the rating. This file joins those measures to the ratings and to
the source condition, and runs what the registration
(`Docs/Preregistration/AsPredicted/Study5_AsPredicted.md`, question 8) names
for the text.

Two checks are registered for creativity:

1. how well the words alone predict the rating and the source condition in
   participants left out of fitting, by ridge regression (section 3.1);
2. whether AI-condition participants reuse their own words across their 18
   justifications more than Human-condition participants, relative to others
   writing about the same second work (section 3.2).

Four items are exploratory, and each is description with no verdict: the
count of Human-condition participants who write that a machine made the work
(4.1), tone and concreteness from published word ratings (4.2), topics found
by a model given no labels (4.3), and the words carrying the rating
prediction (4.4).

Every justification follows its rating, so none of what follows says what
produced a rating. It describes what people wrote once their number was
chosen.

# 1. Setup

## 1.1 Packages

```{r packages}
# readr reads and writes the tables. dplyr, tidyr, tibble and purrr reshape
# them. lme4 and lmerTest fit the mixed models of section 4. Matrix stores
# the word counts sparsely, keeping only the cells that are not zero, and
# glmnet fits the penalised regressions. parallel runs the permutations on
# several processor cores.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readr)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(purrr)
  library(lme4)
  library(lmerTest)
  library(Matrix)
  library(glmnet)
  library(parallel)
})

# The seed the registration names for R.
SEED <- 20260421L
set.seed(SEED)
```

# 2. Load and join

```{r text-manifest}
# Every text file must be the one the notebook's last finished run wrote:
# its SHA-256 must equal the one in the notebook's run manifest.
text_manifest <- read_csv(TEXT_MANIFEST, show_col_types = FALSE, progress = FALSE)
rel_text <- vapply(TEXT_FILES, function(p) relative_path(p, STUDY_DIR), character(1))
listed <- match(rel_text, text_manifest$file)
if (anyNA(listed)) {
  stop("The text run manifest does not list ",
       paste(rel_text[is.na(listed)], collapse = ", "), ".")
}
now_sha <- unname(tools::sha256sum(TEXT_FILES))
if (!identical(now_sha, text_manifest$sha256[listed])) {
  stop("Some text file differs from the one the notebook's run manifest ",
       "records: ", paste(rel_text[now_sha != text_manifest$sha256[listed]],
                          collapse = ", "), ". Rerun Study5_02_Text.ipynb.")
}
cat("Text files match the notebook's run manifest (run ",
    text_manifest$run_id[1], "): TRUE\n", sep = "")
```

```{r load-join}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_text_join_check.csv"))

# The long data. In a blind run label_mode says "shuffled" on every row, and
# the file is refused otherwise; in an unblinded run it must say "real".
long <- read_csv(LONG_TEXT_PATH, col_types = cols(
  id = col_character(), source = col_character(), editing_time = col_character(),
  image = col_character(), image_kind = col_character(), modification = col_character(),
  work_id = col_character(), dimension = col_character(), item = col_character(),
  k_points = col_integer(), rating = col_integer(), rating_01 = col_double(),
  rating_label = col_character(), response_text = col_character(),
  label_mode = col_character()), na = c(""), progress = FALSE)
expected_mode <- if (UNBLIND) "real" else "shuffled"
if (!all(long$label_mode == expected_mode)) {
  stop("The long data says label_mode ", paste(unique(long$label_mode), collapse = ", "),
       ", and this run needs ", expected_mode, ". Knit Study5_01_Quant.Rmd in the ",
       "same mode first.")
}
stopifnot(nrow(long) == 12042, n_distinct(long$id) == 223)

# One row per response. stimulus_id names the second work, the source image
# at one modification level, as in the text tables.
ARM_LEVELS <- c("Human", "AI")
DIMS <- c("transformativeness", "essence_change", "creativity")
ratings <- long %>%
  transmute(id, stimulus_id = work_id, image, image_kind, modification,
            dimension, item, k_points, rating,
            source = factor(source, levels = ARM_LEVELS), editing_time)
stopifnot(!anyNA(ratings$source))

# The measures file, held to its columns. check_text_table() stops if it
# carries the condition, the rating or the text.
MEASURE_COLS <- c("id", "stimulus_id", "stimulus_image", "stimulus_type",
                  "stimulus_modification", "dimension", "n_words",
                  "says_detail", "says_time", "says_skill", "says_concept",
                  "says_prompt", "says_machine_made", "machine_made_reading",
                  "prior_exposure", "anchor_echo", "detail_polarity",
                  "time_polarity", "skill_polarity", "concept_polarity")
FORBIDDEN <- c(TEXT_FORBIDDEN_COLS, "source", "editing_time", "deriv_effort")
measures <- read_csv(TEXT_FILES[["measures"]],
                     col_types = cols(.default = col_character(), n_words = col_integer()),
                     na = character(), progress = FALSE)
check_text_table(measures, MEASURE_COLS, "study5_text_measures.csv", forbidden = FORBIDDEN)

# The join is on participant, second work and question, and must match every
# response exactly once, with the same source image, image kind and
# modification on both sides.
joined <- ratings %>%
  inner_join(measures, by = c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension"),
             relationship = "one-to-one")
stopifnot(all(joined$image == joined$stimulus_image),
          all(joined$image_kind == joined$stimulus_type),
          all(joined$modification == joined$stimulus_modification))
join_check <- tibble(rows_ratings = nrow(ratings), rows_measures = nrow(measures),
                     rows_joined = nrow(joined),
                     ratings_unmatched = nrow(anti_join(ratings, measures,
                                                        by = c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension"))),
                     measures_unmatched = nrow(anti_join(measures, ratings,
                                                         by = c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension"))))
print(as.data.frame(join_check))
stopifnot(join_check$rows_joined == 12042, join_check$ratings_unmatched == 0,
          join_check$measures_unmatched == 0)
write_csv(join_check, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_text_join_check.csv"))
```

# 3. The two registered checks, on creativity

## 3.1 How closely the words track the rating and the source condition

```{r recoverability}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_text_recoverability.csv"))

# text_recoverability() runs the check exactly as Study 1 does. Ridge
# regression, a regression that shrinks every word's weight toward zero,
# predicts the rating and the source condition from the word counts. It is
# scored on participants left out of fitting, in ten folds grouped by
# participant, with a vocabulary floor of five responses applied inside each
# training fold. The rating is scored by the Pearson correlation between
# predicted and observed ratings, and the condition by the AUC, the
# probability that a randomly chosen AI-condition response scores above a
# randomly chosen Human-condition one. Each score has a 95 percent interval
# from resampling participants and a null from 200 permutations, reruns on
# shuffled outcomes. The seed is 20260421.
wordcounts <- read_text_wordcounts(TEXT_FILES[["wordcounts"]])
vocabulary <- read_text_vocabulary(TEXT_FILES[["vocabulary"]])
corpus <- check_text_wordcounts(ratings, wordcounts, vocabulary,
                                stim_cols = "stimulus_id", arm_col = "source",
                                arm_levels = ARM_LEVELS)
print(as.data.frame(corpus))

recover <- text_recoverability(ratings, wordcounts, dims = "creativity",
                               stim_cols = "stimulus_id", arm_col = "source",
                               arm_levels = ARM_LEVELS)
recover <- recover %>%
  left_join(recoverability_readings(recover) %>%
              select(dimension, target, predictors, reading),
            by = c("dimension", "target", "predictors"))
stopifnot(nrow(recover) == 5)
print(as.data.frame(recover %>% select(dimension, target, predictors, estimate,
                                       ci_low, ci_high, null_95th, status, reading) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
write_csv(recover, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_text_recoverability.csv"))
```

## 3.2 Within-person word overlap by source condition

```{r self-overlap}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_text_selfsimilarity_by_arm.csv"))

# text_self_overlap() runs the check exactly as Study 1 does. For each
# participant it takes the mean overlap among their own 18 creativity
# justifications, the Jaccard overlap being the words two texts share divided
# by the words either uses, and subtracts the mean overlap with other
# participants' justifications of the same second work. The difference is
# regressed on the source condition with the mean number of words as a
# covariate. The registration predicts that AI-condition participants reuse
# more, so the AI coefficient is predicted positive. Its interval and p-value
# come from 2,000 resamples of participants within each condition. One
# dimension is registered, so the Holm correction is over one test.
tokens <- read_text_tokens(TEXT_FILES[["tokens"]])
overlap <- text_self_overlap(ratings, tokens, dims = "creativity",
                             stim_cols = "stimulus_id", arm_col = "source",
                             arm_levels = ARM_LEVELS)
by_arm <- overlap$by_arm
stopifnot(sum(by_arm$role == "registered comparison") == 1)
print(as.data.frame(by_arm %>% select(dimension, role, quantity, estimate, ci_lo,
                                      ci_hi, p_raw, p_holm, reading, status) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
write_csv(by_arm, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_text_selfsimilarity_by_arm.csv"))
```

# 4. Exploratory description

The models in sections 4.2 and 4.3 use the five-point items only, as the
primary ratings analysis does, so that the rating they hold constant is on
one scale. Section 4.1 counts every justification.

```{r fit-helpers}
# Every mixed model in this section is fitted through fit_with_status(),
# which keeps whether it stopped with an error, converged or is singular. A
# fit that errored or did not converge carries no p-value. Each fit is
# logged, and the log is written in section 5.
fit_log <- list()
fit_logged <- function(expr, step, d) {
  res <- fit_with_status(expr)
  fit_log[[length(fit_log) + 1]] <<- bind_cols(tibble(step = step, n_obs = nrow(d)),
                                               res$status)
  res
}

# The ratings of the five-point items, with the rating centred within each
# question (the rating minus that question's mean rating). Centring makes the
# source coefficient the AI minus Human difference at the average rating.
ratings5 <- ratings %>% filter(k_points == 5, !is.na(rating))
rating_centres <- ratings5 %>% group_by(dimension) %>%
  summarise(rating_centre = mean(rating), .groups = "drop")
ratings5 <- ratings5 %>% left_join(rating_centres, by = "dimension") %>%
  mutate(rating_c = rating - rating_centre)
CONTROL <- lme4::lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
```

## 4.1 Human-condition participants who write that a machine made the work

```{r machine-made}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_text_machine_made_count.csv"))

# The machine-made reading is "asserted" when a justification states,
# plainly or as an impression, that a machine made the work, and it sets
# aside phrases that are negated or sit in a supposition. The count is of
# Human-condition participants with at least one such justification, over
# all 54 and within each question.
human <- joined %>% filter(source == "Human")
count_scope <- function(d, scope) {
  tibble(scope = scope,
         n_human_participants = n_distinct(d$id),
         n_participants_asserting = n_distinct(d$id[d$machine_made_reading == "asserted"]),
         n_human_responses = nrow(d),
         n_responses_asserted = sum(d$machine_made_reading == "asserted"))
}
machine_count <- bind_rows(
  count_scope(human, "all justifications"),
  bind_rows(lapply(DIMS, function(dm) count_scope(human %>% filter(dimension == dm), dm))))
print(as.data.frame(machine_count))
write_csv(machine_count, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_text_machine_made_count.csv"))
```

## 4.2 Tone and concreteness

```{r affect}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_text_affect_by_arm.csv"))

# Each response's mean valence (how pleasant its words are, 1 to 9), arousal
# (how excited they make a reader feel, 1 to 9), dominance (how much in
# control they make a reader feel, 1 to 9) and concreteness (1 abstract to 5
# concrete), from Warriner et al. (2013) and Brysbaert et al. (2014). A
# response with no matched word has no score and drops out of that model.
#
# The model, per question and measure, as in Study 1:
#   score ~ source * rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)
# with stimulus_id the second work. The two source terms of the twelve
# models are corrected together by the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure, which
# holds the expected share of false positives among the results called
# positive. The correction makes a long table easier to read; it does not
# make it confirmatory.
AFFECT_COLS <- c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension", "n_content_words", "n_vad_matched",
                 "valence", "arousal", "dominance", "n_conc_matched", "concreteness")
affect <- read_csv(TEXT_FILES[["affect"]], col_types = cols(
  id = col_character(), stimulus_id = col_character(), dimension = col_character(),
  .default = col_double()), progress = FALSE)
check_text_table(affect, AFFECT_COLS, "study5_text_affect.csv", forbidden = FORBIDDEN)
affect_joined <- ratings5 %>%
  inner_join(affect, by = c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension"), relationship = "one-to-one")
stopifnot(nrow(affect_joined) == nrow(ratings5))

AFFECT_MEASURES <- c("valence", "arousal", "dominance", "concreteness")
AFFECT_TERMS <- c("sourceAI" = "AI minus Human at the average rating",
                  "sourceAI:rating_c" = "AI minus Human in the slope on the rating")
affect_by_arm <- bind_rows(lapply(DIMS, function(dm) {
  bind_rows(lapply(AFFECT_MEASURES, function(m) {
    d <- affect_joined %>% filter(dimension == dm, !is.na(.data[[m]])) %>%
      mutate(score = .data[[m]])
    res <- fit_logged(lmerTest::lmer(score ~ source * rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
                                     data = d, REML = TRUE, control = CONTROL),
                      paste0("4.2 ", m, ", ", dm), d)
    base <- tibble(dimension = dm, measure = m, term = names(AFFECT_TERMS),
                   quantity = unname(AFFECT_TERMS),
                   mean_Human = mean(d$score[d$source == "Human"]),
                   mean_AI = mean(d$score[d$source == "AI"]),
                   n_scored = nrow(d), converged = res$status$converged,
                   singular = res$status$singular, note = fit_note(res$status))
    if (isTRUE(res$status$fit_error)) return(base)
    co <- as.data.frame(summary(res$fit)$coefficients)[names(AFFECT_TERMS), ]
    base %>% mutate(estimate = co$Estimate, std_error = co$`Std. Error`, df = co$df,
                    t = co$`t value`,
                    p_raw = na_unless_usable(co$`Pr(>|t|)`, res$status))
  }))
}))
affect_by_arm <- affect_by_arm %>%
  mutate(p_bh = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "BH", n = n()), .after = p_raw)
stopifnot(nrow(affect_by_arm) == 24)
print(as.data.frame(affect_by_arm %>% select(dimension, measure, term, estimate, p_raw,
                                             p_bh, n_scored, converged, singular) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
write_csv(affect_by_arm, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_text_affect_by_arm.csv"))
```

## 4.3 Topics

```{r topics}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_text_topics_by_arm.csv"))

# Each response's weight on each topic of the notebook's topic model, fitted
# to each question separately and given no labels. A response's weights sum
# to one. The five heaviest words of each topic label it.
#
# The model, per question and topic, as in Study 1:
#   weight ~ source + rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id)
# Topic weights are bounded between zero and one and pile up at zero, so the
# source term is tested against a permutation null rather than its usual
# standard error. The source labels are dealt out afresh among participants,
# each keeping one label, and the model is refitted. The source term's t value
# is recorded each time, 200 times in all. The p-value is the share of shuffles, counting the
# observed data as one, whose t value is at least as far from zero as the
# observed one. The same 200 shuffles serve every topic in a question, they
# are drawn from the seed before the parallel section starts, and the
# p-values are corrected by Benjamini-Hochberg within each question.
N_TOPIC_PERM <- 200L
topics <- read_csv(TEXT_FILES[["topics"]], col_types = cols(
  id = col_character(), stimulus_id = col_character(), dimension = col_character(),
  topic = col_integer(), weight = col_double()), progress = FALSE)
check_text_table(topics, c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension", "topic", "weight"),
                 "study5_text_topics.csv", forbidden = FORBIDDEN)
top_words <- read_csv(TEXT_FILES[["top_words"]], col_types = cols(
  dimension = col_character(), topic = col_integer(), rank = col_integer(),
  word = col_character(), weight = col_double()), progress = FALSE)
topic_labels <- top_words %>% filter(rank <= 5) %>% arrange(dimension, topic, rank) %>%
  group_by(dimension, topic) %>%
  summarise(topic_label = paste(word, collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")

topics_joined <- topics %>% filter(!is.na(weight)) %>%
  inner_join(ratings5, by = c("id", "stimulus_id", "dimension"))

topic_t <- function(d) {
  fit <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(
    lme4::lmer(weight ~ source + rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
               data = d, REML = TRUE, control = CONTROL))), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(fit)) return(NA_real_)
  co <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  if (!"sourceAI" %in% rownames(co)) return(NA_real_)
  unname(co["sourceAI", "t value"])
}

topics_dimension <- function(dm) {
  d_dim  <- topics_joined %>% filter(dimension == dm)
  id_arm <- d_dim %>% distinct(id, source) %>% arrange(id)
  set.seed(SEED)
  shuffles <- replicate(N_TOPIC_PERM, setNames(sample(as.character(id_arm$source)), id_arm$id),
                        simplify = FALSE)
  bind_rows(lapply(sort(unique(d_dim$topic)), function(k) {
    d <- d_dim %>% filter(topic == k)
    res <- fit_logged(lmerTest::lmer(weight ~ source + rating_c + (1 | id) + (1 | stimulus_id),
                                     data = d, REML = TRUE, control = CONTROL),
                      paste0("4.3 topic ", k, ", ", dm), d)
    usable <- fit_usable(res$status)
    co <- if (isTRUE(res$status$fit_error)) NULL else summary(res$fit)$coefficients
    t_obs <- if (is.null(co)) NA_real_ else unname(co["sourceAI", "t value"])
    t_null <- text_run_permutations(shuffles, function(lab) {
      dd <- d
      dd$source <- factor(lab[dd$id], levels = ARM_LEVELS)
      topic_t(dd)
    }, text_default_workers())
    n_valid <- sum(!is.na(t_null))
    tibble(dimension = dm, topic = k,
           quantity = "AI minus Human in topic weight at the same rating",
           estimate = if (is.null(co)) NA_real_ else unname(co["sourceAI", "Estimate"]),
           t = if (usable) t_obs else NA_real_,
           p_perm = if (!usable || n_valid == 0) NA_real_ else
             (1 + sum(abs(t_null) >= abs(t_obs), na.rm = TRUE)) / (1 + n_valid),
           n_perm = N_TOPIC_PERM, n_perm_valid = n_valid,
           mean_weight_Human = mean(d$weight[d$source == "Human"]),
           mean_weight_AI = mean(d$weight[d$source == "AI"]),
           n_responses = nrow(d), converged = res$status$converged,
           singular = res$status$singular, note = fit_note(res$status))
  })) %>%
    mutate(p_bh = p.adjust(p_perm, method = "BH", n = n()), .after = p_perm)
}

topics_by_arm <- bind_rows(lapply(DIMS, topics_dimension)) %>%
  left_join(topic_labels, by = c("dimension", "topic")) %>%
  relocate(topic_label, .after = topic)
stopifnot(nrow(topics_by_arm) == n_distinct(topics$dimension, topics$topic))
print(as.data.frame(topics_by_arm %>% select(dimension, topic, topic_label, estimate,
                                             p_perm, p_bh, n_perm_valid, converged,
                                             singular) %>%
                      mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ signif(.x, 4)))))
write_csv(topics_by_arm, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_text_topics_by_arm.csv"))
```

## 4.4 The words carrying the rating prediction

```{r prediction-weights}
run_clear_outputs(run, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_text_prediction_weights.csv"))

# The lasso, a penalised regression whose penalty sets most word weights to
# exactly zero, predicts the rating from the word counts, one model per
# question, as in Study 1's rating model. The strength of the penalty is
# chosen by ten-fold cross-validation grouped by participant, with the
# vocabulary floor of five responses applied inside each training fold. The
# choice is lambda.1se, the strongest penalty whose held-out squared error
# is within one standard error of the best. The model is then refitted on
# every response at that penalty, and the words that keep a weight are
# reported with their signs. A positive weight is a word that goes with a
# higher rating. Among words that move together the lasso tends to keep one,
# so a missing word may still go with the rating. None of this tests a word.
lasso_rating_weights <- function(dm) {
  prepared <- prepare_text_ratings(ratings5, "stimulus_id", "source", ARM_LEVELS)
  wc <- wordcounts
  wc$.stim <- stimulus_key(wc, "stimulus_id")
  fr <- text_dimension_frame(prepared, wc, dm)
  resp <- fr$resp
  counts <- fr$counts
  y <- resp$rating

  set.seed(SEED)
  outer_by_id <- text_participant_folds(fr$id_arm, TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS, ARM_LEVELS)
  outer_fold <- unname(outer_by_id[resp$id])

  vocab_all <- text_floor_vocabulary(resp, counts, rep(TRUE, nrow(resp)),
                                     TEXT_WORD_MIN_RESPONSES)
  X_all <- text_response_word_matrix(resp, counts, vocab_all$word)
  fitted <- text_with_warnings(glmnet::glmnet(X_all, y, family = "gaussian", alpha = 1))
  full_fit <- fitted$value
  lam <- full_fit$lambda
  warns <- fitted$warnings

  fold_loss <- matrix(NA_real_, TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS, length(lam))
  fold_n <- integer(TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS)
  for (k in seq_len(TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS)) {
    tr <- outer_fold != k
    Xk <- text_response_word_matrix(
      resp, counts, text_floor_vocabulary(resp, counts, tr, TEXT_WORD_MIN_RESPONSES)$word)
    fk <- text_with_warnings(glmnet::glmnet(Xk[tr, , drop = FALSE], y[tr],
                                            family = "gaussian", alpha = 1, lambda = lam))
    warns <- c(warns, fk$warnings)
    pk <- as.matrix(predict(fk$value, Xk[!tr, , drop = FALSE], s = lam))
    fold_loss[k, ] <- colMeans((y[!tr] - pk)^2)
    fold_n[k] <- sum(!tr)
  }
  cvm <- apply(fold_loss, 2, weighted.mean, w = fold_n)
  cvsd <- sqrt(apply(sweep(fold_loss, 2, cvm)^2, 2, weighted.mean, w = fold_n) /
                 (TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS - 1))
  i_min <- which.min(cvm)
  lambda_1se <- max(lam[cvm <= cvm[i_min] + cvsd[i_min]])
  warns <- unique(warns)

  b <- as.matrix(coef(full_fit, s = lambda_1se))[, 1]
  b <- b[setdiff(names(b), "(Intercept)")]
  b <- b[b != 0]
  words <- if (length(b) == 0) {
    tibble(word = NA_character_, coefficient = NA_real_)
  } else {
    tibble(word = names(b), coefficient = unname(b))
  }
  words %>%
    mutate(dimension = dm, target = "rating", .before = 1) %>%
    mutate(sign = ifelse(coefficient > 0, "positive", "negative"),
           rank = as.integer(rank(-abs(coefficient), ties.method = "first"))) %>%
    left_join(vocab_all %>% rename(n_responses_word = n_responses), by = "word") %>%
    arrange(rank) %>%
    mutate(lambda_1se = lambda_1se, lambda_min = lam[i_min],
           n_words_in_model = nrow(vocab_all), n_nonzero = length(b),
           n_folds = TEXT_N_OUTER_FOLDS, seed = SEED, n_responses = nrow(resp),
           status = if (length(warns) == 0) "ok" else "nonconvergence",
           note = if (length(warns) == 0) "no warning from any fit" else
             paste(warns, collapse = "; "))
}

prediction_weights <- bind_rows(lapply(DIMS, lasso_rating_weights))
for (dm in DIMS) {
  pw <- prediction_weights %>% filter(dimension == dm)
  cat(dm, ": ", pw$n_nonzero[1], " of ", pw$n_words_in_model[1],
      " words keep a weight at lambda.1se (status ", pw$status[1], ").\n", sep = "")
}
write_csv(prediction_weights, file.path(TAB_DIR, "study5_text_prediction_weights.csv"))
```
